criteria.explanation:
The asset claims only requirement candidates and paired binding candidates (statement 23). Every closure rule reads 'Candidate, not ready'. Acceptance stays an owner ruling. The asset claims no release, application closure, continuation or native identity.

It keeps three things apart: construction readiness (req-pressure:24 declines to classify upstream ABI readiness and says any capability that is not ready blocks the dependent edge, with no local compensation); future observed behavior (candidates 11, 12 and 15 describe runs that have not happened); and remaining application obligations (req-pressure:25).

The supplied worksite context is pre-construction, with no revision targets, currentWorksiteDigest null and the observation body omitted. That is consistent with statement 23, which says the supplied context records no subject surface. I could not inventory the worksite independently. Statement 21 honestly says the author used the supplied source without re-hashing it.

pressure.text: In bindings 08 and 09, the verifier_artifact is a design-selected static check (exact import, node:test and strict import, strict-equality assertion). The only verifier_execution named is the planned node --test run, so nothing executes the static check. Design must add an admitted execution of that check. Otherwise the structural verifier_artifact stays unexercised, and the import and strictness properties rest on semantic assessment alone.

Candidate 15's realization is an admitted typed observation, not an authored artifact. req-pressure:23 raises the evidence-model admission question only for candidates 11 and 12, but it applies here too. It is also unassessed whether the installed native-work/observation@5 and command-execution-observation@5 contracts count as the ABI-owned F_P Worker turn that REQ-GLC-WORKSITE-LIFECYCLE-013 requires, one that returns the ordered command results together with exactly one typed helloWorld() observation. If they do not, the dependent edge blocks as an ABI gap.

Candidate 13 requires each predecessor's current digest to be in the dependent's admitted construction basis. The declared dependencyRule reads that basis as declared read paths observed before construction. Under that rule, one construction activation that writes both predecessor and dependent may be unable to satisfy candidate 13, which would make sequential activations a consequence rather than an open option. Design must show whether single-activation satisfaction is possible. The owner ruling on per-turn limits (req-pressure:01) stays open.

These still need an owner ruling, and this assessment grants none:
- whether any per-turn write or no-execution limit survives
- whether traversal-shape parity is still owed
- whether 'artifact summaries' or the artifact bodies form the evidence basis
- who the acceptor is
- whether the direct-return reading of 'returns exactly' should be repriced
- whether assertedReturnValue is a separate declared predicate that needs its own observation

This assessment rests on the supplied source text, predecessor assets and worksite context. I did not re-hash the source member or predecessor assets, and I did not inventory the worksite. I verified candidate-to-identity span links by length only for candidates 01, 02, 03, 13 and 15. The rest were compared by quote content.

Every application obligation is still unrealized:
- all eight file surfaces, each with its derivation basis
- the typed helloWorld() observation
- admitted execution of node --test test/component/hello.test.mjs test/uat/hello.uat.test.mjs, showing per-suite passes, zero failures, at least 2 passes and plan satisfaction (planSatisfied is not yet defined)
- a stdout-match fragment chosen against the real reporter
- design-selected checks for candidates 02-07, 13 and 14
- independent semantic assessment and the owner acceptance ruling

The readiness of the upstream ABI capabilities has not been classified.

Carries product-pressure:01, narrowed. The per-stage "Write only" limits, the "in this vector" bans on earlier stages producing later artifacts, and the plan stage's in-vector no-execution limit are per-turn laws that conflict with the request ruling that the vector mechanism is not runtime authority. The derivation direction they accompany is no longer treated as conflicting; it is normative in requirement-candidate:13. Still unruled: whether derivation direction requires separate sequential construction activations or can be met by one construction that observes each predecessor before writing its dependent. This needs an owner ruling or a design decision within requirement-candidate:13.

Carries product-pressure:02. Whether witness.parityRule (reproduce the eight-step odd_sdlc traversal as typed GTL vectors consumed by ABG startup) is still owed is unruled. It is a builder/runtime concern with no subject requirement, and no current evidence may be claimed as identical traversal. Its ban on copying is carried as requirement-candidate:14.

Carries product-pressure:03. The source names prior "artifact summaries" as the evidence source for the test design, both verifiers and the plan. It does not define a summary or say whether the actual bodies replace summaries under the native lifecycle. Either way, requirement-candidate:13 requires the basis to bind the predecessor's current digest. Unruled.

Carries product-pressure:04. The source does not define how executionStatus, planSatisfied, observedTestPassCount and the stdout digest derive from admitted execution. Nor does it say which digest algorithm applies or what planSatisfied comprises (exact command and args, count floor, zero-failure fragment, asserted return value). requirement-candidate:11 makes that derivation a design-selected verifier artifact over the admitted run record; its content is a design obligation.

Carries product-pressure:05. A count of at least 2 with zero failures does not show that each file contributed a passing test. The admitted runner output, or its derived observations, must attribute passes and failures to test/component/hello.test.mjs and test/uat/hello.uat.test.mjs separately. How the reporter exposes file attribution is unobserved.

Carries product-pressure:06, now made mandatory as requirement-candidate:15 instead of being left conditional. Still open: whether the plan's assertedReturnValue is a separate declared outcome predicate needing its own observation, or is compared against the same one (candidate 15 takes the second reading). The exact typed-observation contract of the consumed ABI is also open.

Carries product-pressure:07. requirement-candidate:01 states the plain reading of "returns exactly": strict equality of the direct return value, which excludes a Promise. The source does not address behavior with arguments, other or default exports, side effects, or what "minimal" excludes. An owner may reprice the direct-return reading.

Carries product-pressure:08. The component and UAT verifiers assert the same value through the same function; the source distinguishes them only by role, file and wording. What else makes UAT distinct is unstated, and no CLI, stdout or other surface may be invented to create a difference.

Carries product-pressure:09. "such as fail 0" is an example. The reporter format of the admitted node executable is unobserved. The fragment must be checked against observed runner output, and the TAP-glyph tolerance must not become tolerance of real failures.
Carries product-pressure:10. The source names no acceptor. Acceptance is an owner ruling over admitted evidence, and this stage cannot assign that authority.
Carries product-pressure:11. Name, version, scripts, dependencies and engines are unconstrained. The source neither permits nor forbids dependency installation.

Carries product-pressure:12. The required ABG-ownership sentence uses predecessor vocabulary (registry selection, graph-call opening, vector traversal). Whether that vocabulary describes the current native lifecycle is unassessed. The sentence is required content, not authority.
Carries product-pressure:13. Beyond the enumerated elements, the content of the three documents is unspecified. Brevity is not compliance, and scope must not expand beyond the source.

Carries product-pressure:14, now carried by requirement-candidate:11. The design document names an execution-result surface that has no file. Design must realize it through admitted native execution and Evidence, never through a result file or prewritten success.

Carries product-pressure:15. executeFromPlan: false lies inside the selected range, but its semantics belong to the sdlcComplianceScenario helper outside it. Classifying it as part of the vector mechanism is an inference. It is in tension with a result judged against observed execution of the plan. No further meaning is inferred.
Carries product-pressure:16. The witness run path, duration and traversal lie outside the readable worksite and were not inspected. They are unverified provenance with no evidence weight.

Carries product-pressure:17. The source names the executable only as node and fixes no version. The current worksite scope declares one executable capability, /opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/24.7.0/bin/node, with cwd root '.'. Its support for node:test, node:assert/strict and ES modules, and its reporter output, are unobserved and belong to design and admitted execution.

The only verifier command the source declares runs the two greeting tests. It does not exercise candidates 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 07, 13 or 14. Design must select verifier artifacts for these or record the gap. A structural check proves presence, not faithfulness, so independent semantic assessment of the actual bodies remains required.

.mjs files load as ES modules whatever package.json type declares, and private has no runtime effect. A passing planned run is therefore no evidence for requirement-candidate:02, which needs its own observation of the actual package.json.

Candidates 01-14 carry the retained requirement identities whose source spans they cover as parentRequirementRefs. Candidate 15 is new and is parented on the greeting and plan identities. Statements and pressure reference retained identities, never same-response candidate refs. Whether admission treats these links as supersession of the retained terms or as refinement children is unassessed. This stage mints no native identity.

The source gives relative subject paths but no subject root. The worksite also holds job and runtime files: the source copy, semantic-assets, the runtime-owned .abiogenesis, and execution-evidence for native Evidence. Design must fix the root, and the inventory checks for candidates 04 and 14 must separate subject content from those files.

The source bans pinning an exact pass-count fragment only "when the generated tests add depth coverage". requirement-candidate:10 keeps that condition. A design that never pins a pass-count fragment is a permitted conservative choice, not a source obligation, and it must still carry zero-failure evidence.

For the file-less execution result and the acceptance predicate, the realization role is filled by admitted run evidence, not an authored artifact. Verifier execution is a separate admitted computation over that evidence. Whether the consumed ABG evidence model admits run evidence in the realization role and the derived-field computation as distinct verifier execution is unassessed and must be confirmed at design.

Proof depends on several ABI-owned capabilities: F_P Worker transport, subject command execution inside that turn, typed outcome observation, evidence admission and assurance fold. This stage does not classify their readiness (ready, missing, placeholder, test_only, unwired, unpinned). Any capability that is not ready blocks the dependent edge and is recorded as an ABI gap. odd_glc adds no harness, stage runner, local module import or execution wrapper to compensate (REQ-GLC-WORKSITE-LIFECYCLE-008; REQ-GLC-ABG-REQUIREMENTS-ALGEBRA-CONSUMPTION-002, -012).

Every application obligation is still unimplemented. That includes all eight surfaces with their derivation bases, the typed outcome observation, and admitted execution of node --test test/component/hello.test.mjs test/uat/hello.uat.test.mjs with per-suite attribution, zero failures, the pass floor of at least 2 and plan satisfaction. report.summary:
Built all 14 selected targets in the order the source and Design set, writing only inside the permitted write scope. I followed the task instruction not to run commands, so none of the tests or checkers has been run. No execution result, result file or success claim was written.

1. `specification/project-conformance.md` states the project-pressure sentence. It lists the seven required downstream surfaces verbatim and includes the ABG-ownership sentence verbatim. A note says that sentence only describes the environment that builds the subject: it grants no authority and puts no runtime machinery in the subject. The document also names itself as the authority for `design/implementation-design.md`.
2. `design/implementation-design.md` has the line 'Authority: specification/project-conformance.md'. It defines `helloWorld()` as a synchronous named export that returns exactly "Hello, world!", with no imports, no default export and no output. It states that `package.json` has exactly `private` and `type`. It names the seven separate surfaces, and says the execution result has no file and is realized only by admitted native execution.
3. `package.json` is exactly `{"private": true, "type": "module"}`, and `src/hello.mjs` has the exact prescribed body.
4. `design/test-design.md` has the line 'Evidence source: package.json and src/hello.mjs'. It gives the component obligation, the UAT obligation (including the phrase 'same exported function'), and the shared constraints: `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`, one `test()` per file, 'component:' and 'uat:' name prefixes, no skip/todo/only/describe/it, and no stdout or CLI surface.
5. `test/component/hello.test.mjs` and `test/uat/hello.uat.test.mjs` have the exact prescribed bodies.
6. `test-execution-plan.json` has the exact prescribed content and no observed-result field.
7. Six read-only checkers in `verification/` use only `node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:url` and `node:crypto`. None imports or executes subject code, spawns a process or writes a file. Each implements every check ID in its Design instruction and prints 'ok'/'not ok' lines, sha256 digests and a summary line, setting `process.exitCode = 1` on any failure. A missing or unparsable file is reported as a failed check, not a crash.
   - `check-verifier-structure` prints the D-suite basis note when both single-test checks pass.
   - `check-derivation` prints a 'construction-basis-not-admitted' note for each edge and a 'derivation-order-not-observable' note.

I checked the prescribed file bodies against every checker rule by reading them, not by running anything, and found no rule they would fail. The only other files in the worksite, apart from `.abiogenesis/` and `semantic-assets/` (both left untouched), are the original source declaration and the 14 targets.

Built all 14 selected targets in the order the source and Design set, writing only inside the permitted write scope. I followed the task instruction not to run commands, so none of the tests or checkers has been run. No execution result, result file or success claim was written.

1. `specification/project-conformance.md` states the project-pressure sentence. It lists the seven required downstream surfaces verbatim and includes the ABG-ownership sentence verbatim. A note says that sentence only describes the environment that builds the subject: it grants no authority and puts no runtime machinery in the subject. The document also names itself as the authority for `design/implementation-design.md`.
2. `design/implementation-design.md` has the line 'Authority: specification/project-conformance.md'. It defines `helloWorld()` as a synchronous named export that returns exactly "Hello, world!", with no imports, no default export and no output. It states that `package.json` has exactly `private` and `type`. It names the seven separate surfaces, and says the execution result has no file and is realized only by admitted native execution.
3. `package.json` is exactly `{"private": true, "type": "module"}`, and `src/hello.mjs` has the exact prescribed body.
4. `design/test-design.md` has the line 'Evidence source: package.json and src/hello.mjs'. It gives the component obligation, the UAT obligation (including the phrase 'same exported function'), and the shared constraints: `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`, one `test()` per file, 'component:' and 'uat:' name prefixes, no skip/todo/only/describe/it, and no stdout or CLI surface.
5. `test/component/hello.test.mjs` and `test/uat/hello.uat.test.mjs` have the exact prescribed bodies.
6. `test-execution-plan.json` has the exact prescribed content and no observed-result field.
7. Six read-only checkers in `verification/` use only `node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:url` and `node:crypto`. None imports or executes subject code, spawns a process or writes a file. Each implements every check ID in its Design instruction and prints 'ok'/'not ok' lines, sha256 digests and a summary line, setting `process.exitCode = 1` on any failure. A missing or unparsable file is reported as a failed check, not a crash.
   - `check-verifier-structure` prints the D-suite basis note when both single-test checks pass.
   - `check-derivation` prints a 'construction-basis-not-admitted' note for each edge and a 'derivation-order-not-observable' note.

I checked the prescribed file bodies against every checker rule by reading them, not by running anything, and found no rule they would fail. The only other files in the worksite, apart from `.abiogenesis/` and `semantic-assets/` (both left untouched), are the original source declaration and the 14 targets.

criteria.explanation: I checked the source file on its own: 6120 bytes, digest sha256:c799b9e4… matches the basis. The stage-0 digest sha256:9f9003ed… also matches. Every sourceQuote in all 15 statements appears exactly once in the source and uses the declared memberRef. I compared each statement against the complete declaration. Statement 01 correctly reads the contract as a return value: the source gives expectedStdout: null and expectedReturnValue "Hello, world!". It adds no CLI or stdout surface. Statement 02 lists all seven downstream surfaces. Statement 03 lists all eight required artifacts and states that the result stage produces no files. Statement 04 covers the conformance content, including the ABG ownership list, and the test-design obligations for both tests. Statement 05 keeps node:test, node:assert/strict and the exact named-export import for both the component and UAT tests. Statement 06 carries all four plan fields exactly, including the floor semantics and the ban on pinning a pass-count fragment. Statement 07 keeps the three acceptance conditions as one conjunction and keeps the TAP-glyph tolerance. Statement 10 records every predecessor dependency correctly: conformance→design, design→source, source→test design, test design and source→component test, component test, test design and source→UAT test, both tests→plan, plan→result. It also records each 'Do not write/materialize' limit. Statements 12 and 14 match the witness fields, the eight-step traversal, the byte range and the scenario identifiers. I found no invented implementation fact or solved requirement. Two small defects do not change the meaning. First, pressure 05 says executeFromPlan: false 'is defined outside the selected range'. The literal is inside the range; only the helper that consumes it is outside. Second, statement 11 counts executeFromPlan as part of the 'stage-vector mechanism', while pressure 05 says it infers no meaning beyond the literal text. The witness runPath value is acknowledged but not quoted. No meaning is lost.

criteria.explanation:
I compared the 23 statements, 15 candidates and 15 bindings with the supplied 6120-byte source text and the admitted Intent and Product assets. I had no file access, so I did not re-hash anything. I spot-checked the cited quotes against the supplied text and found them exact and unique. I also checked, by length, the byte spans that link candidates to requirement identities. Candidate 01 matches the four spans of 30df46b3. Candidate 02 matches the 50-byte and 49-byte spans of 2e3b657b. Candidate 03 matches the spans of d1008669, and candidate 13 matches the seven spans of deb95e34. Candidate 15's four quotes match the grounded spans of db07c18d (154-174, 180-216, 2867-2942, 5411-5457).

The three defects from the previous falsification are repaired.
(1) Candidate 15 restores the typed return-value observation as mandatory, and binding 01 now makes it mandatory rather than conditional. It cites product-pressure:06 and REQ-GLC-WORKSITE-LIFECYCLE-013 accurately: ordered command results plus exactly one typed observation for each declared outcome predicate, inside an ABI-owned F_P turn, with no harness import of the subject module.
(2) Candidate 13 restores the source's authority and evidence relations, with direction. The predecessor must exist when the dependent is built, its current digest must be in the dependent's basis, and a predecessor written afterwards to match does not count. The word "prior" in each source instruction grounds this precedence.
(3) Statement 20 restates the exact runPath and all eight traversal steps, and it still treats step-to-stage matching as inference.

Every source instruction is represented: the eight file surfaces and the file-less result; the three documents' contents; both verifiers' import, node:test/strict and exact assertion; the plan's command, args, floor, zero-failure match, conditional pass-count ban and assertedReturnValue; the judged fields; the conjunctive acceptance rule; and the TAP-glyph tolerance. I found no invented fact. The whole-file digest matches taskData, and statement 21 discloses that the author did not re-hash. I found no material loss, so statement 22's claim holds. Two minor, non-material imprecisions: statement 16 says the turns "each 'Write only' named files", but the result stage says "Produce no files."; and statement 14 no longer restates that the subject is distinct from odd_sdlc, though statements 20-21 and candidate 14 still cover this.

The modality labels are correct. Statements 01-15 are normative, 16-17 conflicting, 18 speculative (depth coverage, neither required nor forbidden) and 19-23 supporting.

Conflicts are kept without being decided:
- The per-turn 'Write only' limits, the 'in this vector' bans, the plan-stage no-execution limit and executeFromPlan: false stay conflicting (statement 16, req-pressure:01).
- executeFromPlan's classification as vector mechanism is explicitly labelled an inference (req-pressure:15).
- The parityRule stays conflicting and unruled (statement 17, req-pressure:02), and no current evidence is claimed as identical traversal. Its ban on copying odd_sdlc machinery is correctly normative as candidate 14.

The derivation direction moved from an open question to normative. That move is justified: the source says "prior", and the Intent assessor required the dependencies to be kept unless an owner rules otherwise. Under that rule, one construction activation that writes both predecessor and dependent may be unable to satisfy candidate 13, which would make sequential activations a consequence rather than an open option. What holds: all 15 active obligations appear, and each has at least one implementation target and one verifier target. I checked all 14 targets, and every bindingVersionRef equals the active version of the obligations that target lists.

Two defects fail the criterion.

(1) The paired proof for the acceptance predicate and the observed result is weakened, and the design does not say so.
- The active binding 0556dad6 (obligation ef532097) needs three things: a design-selected deterministic (F_D) evaluator covering the four conditions, including per-suite attribution; its own admitted execution, separate from the run; and a recorded result for each condition.
- The binding 32722ad5 (obligation 87511aff) needs a deterministic derivation of the per-suite results and of planSatisfied.
- The design supplies C2 predicates only for exit status and the aggregate pass count. Two things are left to 'the Evidence stage … deterministically' (statement 07, design-pressure:02): the component and UAT passes inside planned-verifier-run, and the expectedStdoutMatch comparison.
- The Evidence stage has only the application_assessment capability and must not run tools. So that comparison would be an agent reading the stdout, which is the same act as semantic_assessment. This merges verifier_execution into semantic_assessment for these conditions (C and J must not substitute for each other), and nothing produces the per-condition evaluator record.
- The design records neither the role merge nor a blocking ABI gap (REQ-GLC-WORKSITE-LIFECYCLE-008).
- component-suite-run and uat-suite-run are separate runs and cannot meet 'same run'. The design admits this.
- The source treats planSatisfied as an observed flag; here it becomes a partly deferred composite.

(2) The derivation gap is disclosed for only one of the obligations it affects.

These are disclosed: the naming-only derivation proof, the realization mapping for obligations 7 and 8 (design-pressure:04) and the unclassified typed-observation path (design-pressure:05).

The ABI owns this observation, and it is made in the same native turn as the ordered command results. targets.changeInstruction:
Create the execution plan, derived from both verifier files, with exactly this content:
{
  "command": "node",
  "args": ["--test", "test/component/hello.test.mjs", "test/uat/hello.uat.test.mjs"],
  "expectedTestPassCount": 2,
  "expectedStdoutMatch": "fail 0",
  "assertedReturnValue": "Hello, world!",
  "derivedFrom": ["test/component/hello.test.mjs", "test/uat/hello.uat.test.mjs"]
}

The plan has no observed-result field, and writing it executes nothing.

Create the design-selected verifier for obligations 2, 3, 10 and 13.

General rules:
- Write a Node ES module that uses only node:fs, node:path, node:url and node:crypto.
- The subject root is path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..').
- Only read files. Never import, require or execute src/hello.mjs or any test file, never spawn a process, and never write a file.
- For each check, print exactly 'ok <id>' or 'not ok <id> - <reason>'. For each file read, print 'digest <relative-path> sha256:<hex>'.
- Finish with 'check-inventory: <n> checks, <f> failures', and set process.exitCode = 1 when f > 0.
- A missing or unparsable file is a failed check, never an uncaught crash.

Checks:
(a) surface:<path>: each of specification/project-conformance.md, design/implementation-design.md, package.json, src/hello.mjs, design/test-design.md, test/component/hello.test.mjs, test/uat/hello.uat.test.mjs and test-execution-plan.json is a non-empty regular file.
(b) exact-set:<dir>: the recursive file listings equal exactly:
- specification/{project-conformance.md}
- design/{implementation-design.md, test-design.md}
- src/{hello.mjs}
- test/{component/hello.test.mjs, uat/hello.uat.test.mjs}
- verification/{check-inventory.mjs, check-package.mjs, check-documents.mjs, check-verifier-structure.mjs, check-plan.mjs, check-derivation.mjs}
(c) no-authored-result: no file in those directories or at the root has a basename matching /execution[-_ ]?result/i.
(d) root-entries:
- The root contains no node_modules and no bin.
- The allowed root entries are .abiogenesis, semantic-assets, execution-evidence, original-js-sdlc-bootstrap-declaration.txt, package.json, test-execution-plan.json, specification, design, src, test and verification.
- Any other root entry fails if its name matches /\.(m?js|cjs|sh)$|result|ledger|registry|controller|scheduler/i. Otherwise print 'note <name>'.
- Never descend into .abiogenesis, semantic-assets or execution-evidence.
(e) no-copied-machinery:
- src/hello.mjs contains no \bimport\b token and no 'require(' token.
- None of package.json, src/hello.mjs, the two verifiers or the plan contains any of the following, case-insensitively: odd_sdlc, abiogenesis, ledger, registry, controller, scheduler, child_process, node:net, node:http.
- The three documents are exempt from (e).

Create the design-selected verifier for obligations 2, 7, 8, 10 and 11.

General rules:
- Write a Node ES module that uses only node:fs, node:path, node:url and node:crypto.
- The subject root is path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..').
- Read files as text only. Never import or execute the test files or src/hello.mjs, never spawn a process, and never write a file.
- Print 'ok <id>' or 'not ok <id> - <reason>' for each check, and 'digest <path> sha256:<hex>' for each file read.
- Finish with 'check-verifier-structure: <n> checks, <f> failures', and set process.exitCode = 1 when f > 0.
- A missing file is a failed check.

Run the following checks for suite 'component' (file test/component/hello.test.mjs, prefix 'component:') and for suite 'uat' (file test/uat/hello.uat.test.mjs, prefix 'uat:'). Substring checks are exact unless noted:
- <suite>-node-test: contains 'import { test } from "node:test"'.
- <suite>-assert-strict: contains 'import assert from "node:assert/strict"'.
- <suite>-exact-import: contains 'import { helloWorld } from "../../src/hello.mjs"'.
- <suite>-import-set: every specifier captured by /from\s+["']([^"']+)["']/g or /import\(\s*["']([^"']+)["']/g is one of node:test, node:assert/strict, ../../src/hello.mjs.
- <suite>-resolves-to-subject: path.resolve(path.dirname(file), '../../src/hello.mjs') equals path.join(root, 'src/hello.mjs'), and that file exists.
- <suite>-strict-assertion: contains 'assert.strictEqual(helloWorld(), "Hello, world!")'.
- <suite>-name-prefix: contains 'test("' immediately followed by the prefix.
- <suite>-single-test: /\btest\(/g matches exactly once.
- <suite>-no-other-test-forms: contains neither 'describe(' nor 'suite(', and /\bit\(/ does not match.
- <suite>-no-skip-or-focus: contains none of 'skip', 'todo', '.only' (case-insensitive).
- <suite>-no-doubles-or-output: contains none of 'console.', 'process.', 'stdout', 'child_process', 'mock'.

Then run two cross-file checks:
- verifiers-distinct: the two files have different sha256 digests.
- verifiers-total-tests: the /\btest\(/g matches across both files total exactly 2.

Finally, when both single-test checks pass, print 'note suite-attribution-basis component=1 uat=1'. This line is the static basis of rule D-suite. It is not an observation of any run.

General rules:
- Write a Node ES module that uses only node:fs, node:path, node:url and node:crypto.

- Finish with 'check-plan: <n> checks, <f> failures', and set process.exitCode = 1 when f > 0.
- A missing or unparsable file is a failed check.

Constants:
- PLANNED_ARGS = ['--test','test/component/hello.test.mjs','test/uat/hello.uat.test.mjs'], the design's literal planned-verifier-run arguments.
- PASS_FLOOR_LITERAL = 2, the literal of the planned-run-pass-floor predicate.
- EXPECTED_RETURN_VALUE = 'Hello, world!', the source's expectedReturnValue.

Checks on test-execution-plan.json:
- plan-parses: the file parses as JSON.
- plan-command: command === 'node'.
- plan-args: args deep-equals PLANNED_ARGS.
- plan-args-exist: both listed files exist.
- plan-pass-floor: expectedTestPassCount is an integer >= 2.
- plan-pass-floor-achievable: expectedTestPassCount <= the total number of /\btest\(/g matches across the two verifier files.
- plan-pass-floor-matches-predicate: expectedTestPassCount === PASS_FLOOR_LITERAL.
- plan-stdout-match: expectedStdoutMatch is a string that contains 'fail 0'.
- plan-no-pass-pin: expectedStdoutMatch does not match /pass\s*\d/i.
- plan-asserted-return-value: assertedReturnValue === EXPECTED_RETURN_VALUE.
- plan-no-observed-result: none of the keys executionStatus, planSatisfied, observedTestPassCount, stdoutDigest, observedReturnValue, result or results is present.
